course.title: Solidity — Smart Contract Programming from Beginner to Professional Practice
course.description: A visual-first, version-aware Solidity course based on the supplied 300-topic curriculum. It progresses from blockchain and language foundations through standards, EVM internals, defensive security, testing, gas analysis, deployment, upgradeability, cross-chain assumptions, and professional engineering.
course.version_scope: Examples target the Solidity compiler v0.8.37 release as listed in the official release repository on 2026-10-20. The PDF includes a “0.8.38-…” reference associated with development documentation; do not treat that as a stable compiler version. Re-check release notes, compiler bugs, library versions, and target-network support before publication.
audience: programming learners interested in Ethereum-compatible smart contracts
students learning token standards and decentralized applications
engineers studying smart contract testing, security, and protocol architecture
prerequisites: Essential: variables, conditions, loops, functions, and basic data structures.
Recommended: JavaScript or Python fundamentals, Git/command-line familiarity, and basic blockchain transaction concepts.
Learners new to programming should complete an introductory programming course before advanced modules.
learning_outcomes: Explain blockchain execution, Ethereum accounts, transactions, gas, and EVM behavior.
Write, compile, test, and debug Solidity contracts using functions, data types, state, events, errors, inheritance, and interfaces.
Build standard-based token and application contracts with reviewed reusable libraries.
Integrate contracts with JavaScript applications, wallets, RPC endpoints, and event indexing workflows.
Use unit, negative, fuzz, and invariant tests and interpret gas measurements.
Identify common smart contract risks and apply defensible authorization, validation, and external-call practices.
Reproduce builds, deploy to local/test networks, verify source where supported, and document limitations.

overview_visual.alt_text: Six-stage Solidity course roadmap from foundations through core language, EVM/application standards, security/testing, production engineering and advanced specialization.
overview_visual.caption: Move from foundations to advanced specializations after demonstrating the milestone in each stage.
